correctness.rationale: All 1052 possible valid matching faces were exhaustively enumerated independently by bit-mask DP and recursive include/exclude. The specified staged toggling pairs all but 16 three-simplices in the augmented poset; after retaining the singleton from the empty-face pair, there are exactly 517 ordinary pairs, one critical vertex and 16 critical three-cells. Every one of the 3744 ordinary Hasse cover arrows was built and the acyclic orientation topologically sorted all 1051 nodes. Forman discrete Morse yields a CW model with only one 0-cell and sixteen 3-cells, hence an integral wedge of 16 S^3. Independent mod-2/mod-3 chain ranks corroborate. The complete 12-element automorphism group was obtained by exact backtracking; explicit D6 generators reproduce it. Signed Lefschetz chain traces give the class character (16,0,-2,0,-2,0) on rotations, zero on reflections, with integral nonnegative multiplicities 1,1,1,1,3,3. This proves the rational character, not an integral group-lattice decomposition.

value.rationale: The Tietze graph is a canonical 12-vertex cubic, nonplanar, almost-Hamiltonian graph, naturally constructed by inflating a Petersen vertex to a triangle. Ordinary matching complexes encode all compatible partial edge choices; their integral homotopy type is not reducible to counting perfect matchings. The full 16-sphere classification, despite nonpure simplices reaching dimension five, supplies a non-obvious exact topological invariant. The complete dihedral character provides a meaningful additional symmetry refinement invisible to Betti numbers and determines the multiplicities of all six rational irreducible representations. Its specificity is justified by the graph’s canonical role and the contrast with the related Petersen construction; no family-level significance is overstated.
